correctness.rationale: For every integer n>=4, the spherical Blaschke–Petkantschin coarea factor (1-h^2) times the all-other-sites cap probability ((1+h)/2)^(n-3) gives U=(1+h)/2~Beta(n-1,2). Unit-circumradius shape has density proportional to s=sin(x)sin(y)sin(x+y); the area is (1-h^2)2s and acuteness is x,y,pi-x-y<pi/2. The six exact J_p integrals were independently evaluated by symbolic integration, checked by high-precision quadrature, and multiplied by exact beta moments and deterministic 2n-4 facet count. Direct n=4/5/9 convex-hull simulations agree but are not relied on as infinite proof. Boundary equalities have probability zero.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2020 Akopyan–Edelsbrunner–Nikitenko paper already has the half-acute count fraction, independent shape-size decomposition, expected total area, and general intensity functional; these are not claimed new. The explicitly evaluated 1/4+4/pi^2 and 53/70 metric acute fractions and matching exact squared-area finite-n totals are absent from the inspected full text, as from the height-only Bonnet–O’Reilly and Finch angle-density sources. Closely ranked published results concern different facets/objects or different metrics, and accessible prior claim text has no equivalent. The originality is an explicit natural metric evaluation rather than a new coarea theorem; historical priority, including older Poisson–Delaunay tables, remains a stated residual risk.
residual_risks: The prior shape/size factorization and full typical-facet intensity permit deriving these values by specializing and evaluating integrals; historical originality of the explicit evaluations should be independently checked.
Older specialized Poisson–Delaunay moment tables may evaluate acute-conditioned area moments in unindexed passages; the Finch document was not completely inspected as a rendered PDF.
Semantic literature and database searches cannot establish exhaustive historical priority.

value.rationale: Annealed Euclidean facet area and squared-area mass are two natural triangulation-quality observables, sensitive to large faces and distinguished from count by the unexpectedly exact 1/4+4/pi^2 and 53/70 acute shares, constant for all finite n>=4. The complete finite-n squared-area moment adds a natural quantitative variance-sensitive invariant. The object and weight choices precede the computation and are not arbitrary numerical slices; no downstream theorem is required.
